## Body heating, top cooling and bottom heating (`body-heat`, `top-cool`, `bot-heat`) {#sec-ch09-heating}

### Summary

These three modules are prescribed heat sources for idealised convection. They touch only the total energy, so
they change the temperature and, through it, the pressure; mass and momentum are untouched. `body-heat` is a
volumetric rate; `top-cool` and `bot-heat` stand for a radiative or surface flux at the top or bottom of the
domain.

Each boundary flux can name its layer in either of two ways, and they behave differently. `depth`[^rg-88dfb371d25d] counts cells,
so the layer is as thick as whatever cells happen to sit at that end, and only the block that owns the physical
$x_1$ boundary forces. `thickness`[^rg-74f4a55744e4] is the length of that layer in $x_1$ units: each cell takes the part of the
layer that lies inside it, and every block does so, so a layer that reaches past one block is continued into the next. On a
grid whose $x_1$ cells are not all the same width, `depth` delivers the wrong column total and `thickness`
delivers the right one; on such a grid `depth` is refused outright.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** `body-heat` heats every interior cell whose pressure lies in a band at a fixed rate of temperature
change at constant volume; `top-cool` and `bot-heat` remove or add a fixed energy flux, spread over the top or
bottom `depth` cells or over a layer of `thickness` in $x_1$ length; @eq-ch09-heating-body,
@eq-ch09-heating-flux and @eq-ch09-heating-layer.

**Data.** In: density, pressure, $c_v$, heat rate or boundary flux, and either a depth in cells or a thickness in
metres with the $x_1$ faces; out: the stage energy increment.

**Placement.** Every RK stage, in the forcing loop; with `depth` only on the block that owns the physical $x_1$
boundary, with `thickness` on every block.

**Activation.** `forcing/body-heat: {dTdt, pmin, pmax}`, defaults 0, 0, 1 [$\mathrm{K\,s^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{Pa}$,
$\mathrm{Pa}$]; `top-cool: {flux, depth | thickness}`, `flux` $\le0$; `bot-heat: {flux, depth | thickness}`,
`flux` $\ge0$; defaults `flux` 0, `depth` 1 cell and `thickness` 0, which means "use `depth`"
[$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$, cells, m]. Each off unless its key is present.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact pointwise sources; with `depth` the column receives exactly $F$ only on uniform
cells, with `thickness` on any $x_1$ grid; neither is corrected for a curved cell volume; the default `pmax` of 1
$\mathrm{Pa}$ heats almost nothing.

**Evidence.** Report checks and source-test assertions are listed below; solver ctests were not run at the pin.
:::

**Data details.** In: the interior density $\rho$, pressure $p$[^rg-6691bc383516] [$\mathrm{Pa}$] and mixture $c_v$ (`body-heat`); the
flux $F$ [$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$], `depth` and the $x_1$ width `dz` of the boundary cell, or `thickness` with the
block's $x_1$ faces and the global $x_1$ bounds (`top-cool`, `bot-heat`); $\Delta t$.
Out: the energy row of the increment, per unit volume [$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$]. Check cases: $F=-30$
$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$ with `depth` 4 on uniform cells and on cells growing upward by 10 %, and the same flux with
`thickness` 230 m, 7 m and the whole column on three grids.

**Evidence details.** Tests: heating only inside the pressure band with the mixture $c_v$,
{{< code tests/test_forcing.cpp forcing.body_heat_uses_pressure_mask_and_mixture_cv >}}; linearity of the boundary
fluxes in $\Delta t$, {{< code tests/test_forcing.cpp forcing.boundary_fluxes_scale_with_timestep >}} (both
`allclose` defaults); these ctests were not run at the pin. The only solver test of a delivered column total is
the layer-form one of @tbl-ch09-heating-tests; the `depth` form has none. Check:
`python3 src/snapy_report/ch09/checks/heating_check.py`, output `heating_check.out` lines `[C1]`–`[C5]`, re-run at
the pin: all five PASS, `[C1]`–`[C3]` with the digits they had before [^env-heating].

Local symbols: $\dot T$ [K s$^{-1}$] the heating rate `dTdt`; $p_{\min}$, $p_{\max}$ [Pa]
the pressure band; $F$ [W m$^{-2}$] the boundary flux `flux`; $n_{\mathrm{dep}}$ the number of cells `depth` it is spread
over (appendix A does not use a bare $d$); $\Delta x_{1,\mathrm b}$ [m] the $x_1$ width of the boundary cell, `dz`;
$\overline{\Delta x_1}$ [m] the mean $x_1$ width of the $n_{\mathrm{dep}}$ cells; $L$ [m] the layer `thickness` and
$\lambda_i$ [m] the length of cell $i$ that lies inside that layer; $E_{\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_iE_iV_i$ [J] the integrated total
energy. $\rho$, $p$, $c_v$, $E$, $\Delta t$ and $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ are defined in @sec-appa.

The default `pmax` is 1 $\mathrm{Pa}$: a `body-heat` block that does not set `pmin` and `pmax` heats only cells with
$0\le p\le1$ $\mathrm{Pa}$, which in most decks is none.

### Derivation

*Body heating.* At constant volume the internal energy density changes by $\rho c_v\,\mathrm{d}T$, so a heating rate
$\dot T$ adds, in one stage and in every interior cell with $p_{\min}\le p_i\le p_{\max}$,

$$
\Delta E_i = \Delta t\,\dot T\,\rho_ic_{v,i} ,
$$ {#eq-ch09-heating-body}

with $c_v$ the mixture value of the equation of state at the cell's state, in `BodyHeatImpl::forward`
({{< code src/forcing/body_heat.cpp BodyHeatImpl::forward >}}). For a constant $c_v$ at fixed density this raises
$T$ by exactly $\dot T\Delta t$;[^heat-c3] a $c_v$ that depends on $T$ makes it first order in $\Delta t$.

*Boundary fluxes.* A flux $F$ [$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$] spread over the $n_{\mathrm{dep}}$ cells next to the boundary is applied to
each of those cells as a uniform volumetric rate

$$
\Delta E_i = \Delta t\,\frac{F}{\Delta x_{1,\mathrm b}\,n_{\mathrm{dep}}} ,
$$ {#eq-ch09-heating-flux}

<!-- equation-check: eq-ch09-heating-flux ch09_dropin_check.py [D2] -->

with $\Delta x_{1,\mathrm b}$ the $x_1$ width of the boundary cell, `dz`, in `TopCoolImpl::forward`
({{< code src/forcing/top_cool.cpp TopCoolImpl::forward >}}) and `BotHeatImpl::forward`
({{< code src/forcing/bot_heat.cpp BotHeatImpl::forward >}}). What the column receives follows in three steps.

1. *Per cell.* Each of the $n_{\mathrm{dep}}$ cells gains @eq-ch09-heating-flux, the same value in every cell.
2. *Per unit horizontal area.* On a Cartesian grid a cell's energy is $E_i\Delta x_{1,i}$ per unit area, so the column
   gains $\sum_i\Delta E_i\,\Delta x_{1,i} = \Delta t\,F\,n_{\mathrm{dep}}\overline{\Delta x_1}/(\Delta x_{1,\mathrm b}n_{\mathrm{dep}})
   = \Delta t\,F\,\overline{\Delta x_1}/\Delta x_{1,\mathrm b}$.
3. *Hence* exactly $F$ per unit time on uniform cells (`[C1]`), and $F\,\overline{\Delta x_1}/\Delta x_{1,\mathrm b}$ otherwise: 0.872 for
   cells growing upward by 10 % with $n_{\mathrm{dep}}=4$ (`[C2]`).[^heat-c12]

*The layer form.* With `thickness` the layer is a fixed interval of $x_1$ of length $L$ measured from the global
domain end, $[x_{1,\min},x_{1,\min}+L]$ for `bot-heat` and $[x_{1,\max}-L,x_{1,\max}]$ for `top-cool`. Write
$\lambda_i$ for the length of cell $i$ inside it,

$$
\lambda_i = \max\Bigl(0,\ \min(x_{1,i+1/2},\,x_{1,\max})-\max(x_{1,i-1/2},\,x_{1,\max}-L)\Bigr)
$$ {#eq-ch09-heating-overlap}

for `top-cool`, and its mirror image for `bot-heat`. The energy the cell receives is the flux in one stage times
that cell's share of the layer, spread over the cell's own width,

$$
\Delta E_i = \Delta t\,\frac{F}{L}\,\frac{\lambda_i}{\Delta x_{1,i}} ,
$$ {#eq-ch09-heating-layer}

in `TopCoolImpl::forward` ({{< code src/forcing/top_cool.cpp TopCoolImpl::forward >}}) and `BotHeatImpl::forward`
({{< code src/forcing/bot_heat.cpp BotHeatImpl::forward >}}). The column total follows in two steps.

1. *Per unit horizontal area.* On a Cartesian grid cell $i$ contributes $\Delta E_i\,\Delta x_{1,i} =
   \Delta t\,F\lambda_i/L$.
2. *The overlaps tile the layer.* The $\lambda_i$ are the lengths of disjoint pieces that cover
   $[x_{1,\max}-L,x_{1,\max}]$ exactly, so $\sum_i\lambda_i = L$ whenever the layer lies inside the column, which
   the setup check guarantees, and the sum is $\Delta t\,F$ on **any** $x_1$ grid. Measured at
   $8.9\times10^{-16}$ of $F\Delta t$ over three grids and three thicknesses (`[C4]`), and a cell takes its own
   overlap and nothing more: a layer half as thick as the end cell heats that cell alone, and a layer that reaches
   a quarter of the way into the next cell gives it exactly that quarter's share (`[C5]`).

The two forms differ in one more way. @eq-ch09-heating-flux is applied only by the block that owns the physical
$x_1$ boundary, so a `depth` that reaches past that block is lost; @eq-ch09-heating-layer is applied by every
block from the global bounds, so a layer that spans an $x_1$ split is continued. Neither form corrects for the
cell volume of a curved grid, where $V_i$ is not $\Delta x_{1,i}$ times a fixed area.

*Round-off.* The per-cell value `dt * flux / (dz * depth)` carries three roundings (the two products and the
division), so it is within $3\cdot\tfrac{\epsilon_{\mathrm m}}2$ relative of $\Delta t\,F/(\Delta x_{1,\mathrm b}n_{\mathrm{dep}})$, and the
delivered column energy within the same relative bound (check: at most 0.870 of it). Adding it into the energy
row adds one more rounding of the row's new value, $\tfrac{\epsilon_{\mathrm m}}2\lvert\Delta E_i^{\mathrm{new}}\rvert$, which is relative to the
whole increment of the cell, not to the heating. The layer form's per-cell value
`dt * flux / thickness * overlap / dx1f` carries four roundings and the two clamps of @eq-ch09-heating-overlap are
exact, so the same bound holds with $4\cdot\tfrac{\epsilon_{\mathrm m}}2$. On a spherical-polar grid the cell volume is not $\Delta x_1$ times a fixed area, so the
delivered power is not $F$ either, in either form; not measured.

*Exact and truncated.* Both sources are exact pointwise for the stage-entry state; nothing is truncated in space.

[^heat-c3]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch09/checks/heating_check.py`, output `heating_check.out`, line `[C3]`; a numpy port
    of the three `forward` functions at the pin, double precision.
[^heat-c12]: Same command, lines `[C1]` (uniform cells: $-30$ $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$ delivered for $F=-30$, $n_{\mathrm{dep}}=4$) and
    `[C2]` (ratio 0.871713); `[C4]` and `[C5]` are the layer form, in the same run and the same output file.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch09-heating-column shows where each module acts.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch09-heating-column
#| fig-cap: "Where the three heating modules act in an $x_1$ column bounded by walls (thick black lines). Blue: the top $n_{\\mathrm{dep}}$ cells cooled by top-cool, a flux $F\\le0$ in $\\mathrm{W\\,m^{-2}}$; vermillion: the bottom $n_{\\mathrm{dep}}$ cells heated by bot-heat, $F\\ge0$; orange: the cells inside the pressure band $p_{\\min}\\le p\\le p_{\\max}$ (in $\\mathrm{Pa}$) of body-heat; light blue: untouched cells."
#| fig-alt: "A vertical stack of ten cells with the top three, the bottom two and three middle cells shaded, each labelled with the module and its formula."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch09.figures.fig_heating_column import make_fig
make_fig()
```

All three are cell sources: no stencil and no ghosts are read. `body-heat` acts on interior cells only.
`top-cool` and `bot-heat` slice only in $x_1$, so they also write the $x_2$, $x_3$ ghost cells of their rows, which
the boundary fill overwrites. They run in every stage, explicit, in the forcing loop (@sec-ch09-framework).

The layer form reads the block's own interior $x_1$ faces and the mesh's global $x_1$ bounds, so each block
computes its overlap with the same layer and no communication is needed. It writes the interior $x_1$ cells of the
block, which is the whole of a block that lies inside the layer and none of a block outside it.

### Code

**A minimal input.** Convection driven from below and cooled from above:

```yaml
forcing:
  bot-heat: {flux: 30., depth: 2}            # W m^-2 >= 0, spread over the 2 bottom cells
  top-cool: {flux: -30., depth: 2}           # W m^-2 <= 0
  body-heat: {dTdt: 1.e-5, pmin: 5.e4, pmax: 1.e5}   # K s^-1 inside 0.5-1 bar; pmax defaults to 1 Pa
```

On a grid whose $x_1$ cells are not all the same width, name the layer in metres instead:

```yaml
forcing:
  bot-heat: {flux: 30., thickness: 230.}     # W m^-2 >= 0, over the bottom 230 m of x1
  top-cool: {flux: -30., thickness: 7.}      # W m^-2 <= 0, over the top 7 m
```

**What is refused, and why.**

1. *An unknown key* in each block, by `check_keys`.
2. *`pmin` > `pmax`*, with "BodyHeatOptions: pmin must not exceed pmax." ({{< code src/forcing/body_heat.cpp >}}): the band would be empty.
3. *A positive `top-cool` flux*, with "TopCool flux must be negative" ({{< code src/forcing/top_cool.cpp >}}; zero is accepted), and a
   negative `bot-heat` flux, with "BotHeat flux must be positive" ({{< code src/forcing/bot_heat.cpp >}}; zero is accepted): each
   module has one direction.
4. *`depth` $\le0$*, with "TopCool depth must be greater than zero" or "BotHeat depth must be greater than zero"
   ({{< code src/forcing/top_cool.cpp >}}, {{< code src/forcing/bot_heat.cpp >}}).
5. *Both `depth` and `thickness` in one block*, with "TopCool: give depth (cells) or thickness (x1 length), not
   both" ({{< code src/forcing/top_cool.cpp TopCoolOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}) and the `BotHeat` mirror
   ({{< code src/forcing/bot_heat.cpp BotHeatOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}): the two name the layer in different
   units and the code would silently take one.
6. *A `thickness` that is not finite and positive*, when the key is present, with "TopCool thickness must be
   finite and greater than zero" ({{< code src/forcing/top_cool.cpp TopCoolOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}) and the
   `BotHeat` mirror. An absent key leaves `thickness` at 0, which selects the `depth` form.
7. *A `thickness` longer than the $x_1$ column*, $L > x_{1,\max}-x_{1,\min}$, with "[TopCool] thickness exceeds
   the x1 column" ({{< code src/forcing/top_cool.cpp TopCoolImpl::reset >}}) and the `BotHeat` mirror
   ({{< code src/forcing/bot_heat.cpp BotHeatImpl::reset >}}): otherwise step 2 of the layer derivation fails and
   the column would receive less than $F$.
8. *`depth` on a grid that declares a stretched $x_1$*, with "an integer depth is not supported on a stretched x1
   ... it counts cells; give thickness, the layer in x1 length units"
   ({{< code src/forcing/bot_heat.cpp BotHeatImpl::reset >}},
   {{< code src/forcing/top_cool.cpp TopCoolImpl::reset >}}). The refusal is the setup-time form of the first item
   of the Limits layer: on unequal cells the `depth` form delivers the wrong column total, so the deck must say
   what it means in metres. A curved grid with equal radial widths is **not** caught by this check, because
   `stretched_x1` is a property of the grid key and not of the cell volumes
   ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::stretched_x1 >}}).

**The code, mapped to @eq-ch09-heating-body and @eq-ch09-heating-flux:**

```cpp
// BodyHeatImpl::forward
auto mask =
    torch::logical_and(pres >= options->pmin(), pres <= options->pmax());
du[IPR].index(interior) += torch::where(mask, dt * options->dTdt() * rho * cv,
                                        torch::zeros_like(pres));
// TopCoolImpl::forward
if (!phydro->pmb->options->is_physical_boundary(0, 0, 1)) return du;
auto dz = pcoord->dx1f[iu];
du[IPR].slice(-1, iu + 1 - options->depth(), iu + 1) +=
    dt * options->flux() / (dz * options->depth());
```

`mask` is $p_{\min}\le p_i\le p_{\max}$ and the `where` line @eq-ch09-heating-body; `dz` is $\Delta x_{1,\mathrm b}$ of the top cell
and the last line @eq-ch09-heating-flux on the top $n_{\mathrm{dep}}$ cells. `BotHeatImpl::forward` is the mirror image with
`narrow(-1, il, depth)` and `dx1f[il]`.

The layer branch runs first and returns, so the `is_physical_boundary` test above is never reached with a
`thickness` set ({{< code src/forcing/top_cool.cpp TopCoolImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
// TopCoolImpl::forward
if (options->thickness() > 0.) {
  int il = pcoord->il(), iu = pcoord->iu();
  double hi = pcoord->options->global_x1max();
  double lo = hi - options->thickness();
  auto xf = pcoord->x1f.slice(0, il, iu + 2);
  auto overlap =
      (xf.slice(0, 1).clamp_max(hi) - xf.slice(0, 0, -1).clamp_min(lo)).clamp_min(0.);
  du[IPR].slice(-1, il, iu + 1) += dt * options->flux() /
                                   options->thickness() * overlap /
                                   pcoord->dx1f.slice(0, il, iu + 1);
  return du;
}
```

`overlap` is $\lambda_i$ of @eq-ch09-heating-overlap, with the two `clamp` calls the $\min$ and the $\max$ and
`clamp_min(0.)` the outer $\max(0,\cdot)$; the `+=` line is @eq-ch09-heating-layer.

: Code map of the heating modules. {#tbl-ch09-heating-code}

1. Each `from_yaml` checks its keys and values: `pmin` $\le$ `pmax` for `body-heat`, the sign of `flux`, a
   positive `depth`, at most one of `depth` and `thickness`, and a finite positive `thickness` when it is given,
   for the two boundary fluxes
   ({{< code src/forcing/body_heat.cpp BodyHeatOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}},
   {{< code src/forcing/top_cool.cpp TopCoolOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}},
   {{< code src/forcing/bot_heat.cpp BotHeatOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
2. `TopCoolImpl::reset` and `BotHeatImpl::reset` see the coordinate for the first time and apply the two checks
   that need it: a stretched $x_1$ must use `thickness`, and `thickness` must fit inside the $x_1$ column
   ({{< code src/forcing/top_cool.cpp TopCoolImpl::reset >}},
   {{< code src/forcing/bot_heat.cpp BotHeatImpl::reset >}}).
3. `BodyHeatImpl::forward` masks the interior by the pressure band and adds @eq-ch09-heating-body
   ({{< code src/forcing/body_heat.cpp BodyHeatImpl::forward >}}).
4. `TopCoolImpl::forward` and `BotHeatImpl::forward` add @eq-ch09-heating-layer on every block and return, when a
   `thickness` is set; otherwise they return at once unless the block's upper or lower $x_1$ face is physical, and
   then add @eq-ch09-heating-flux ({{< code src/forcing/top_cool.cpp TopCoolImpl::forward >}},
   {{< code src/forcing/bot_heat.cpp BotHeatImpl::forward >}}).

**Evidence.** The check numbers come from the port named in the footnotes. ctest cases: **pending a pinned ctest
run**.
**Coverage.** CPU only. `heat_layer_deposits_flux_dt` is the one solver test of a delivered column total, and it

:::

### Limits

1. **Stretched cells, `depth` form.** @eq-ch09-heating-flux uses the boundary cell's width for all $n_{\mathrm{dep}}$ cells, so the delivered
   power is $F$ only on uniform cells (`[C2]`). A deck that declares a stretched $x_1$ is refused at setup and must
   use `thickness`; a deck whose cells are unequal for another reason, a curved grid or an $x_1$ split with
   unequal block widths, is not refused and carries the error silently.
2. **Curved grids, both forms.** No correction for the cell volume of spherical-polar or cubed-sphere grids: the
   column argument divides by $\Delta x_{1,i}$, which is the cell volume per unit area only on a Cartesian grid.
   Not measured for either form.
3. **`depth` against the block.** `depth` is checked to be positive but not against the block's $x_1$ cell count;
   the `depth` cells are taken in the block that owns the boundary, and no other block applies the flux, so under
   an $x_1$ split a `depth` that reaches past that block is not continued into the next. A `depth` beyond the interior can select ghost cells with `top-cool`;
   `bot-heat` throws when its `narrow` extends beyond the allocated tensor. Keep `depth` within the interior.
   `thickness` has neither defect: it is checked against the whole column and every block applies it.
4. **The layer is measured from the global bound, not from a wall.** @eq-ch09-heating-layer uses
   `global_x1min` and `global_x1max`, so it heats the layer next to the end of the domain whatever the boundary
   condition there is. With an outflow or periodic $x_1$ boundary that is still what it does; nothing warns.
5. **`thickness` and `depth` are not interchangeable in a restart.** Switching a deck between the two changes
   which cells are forced and, on unequal cells, the delivered total; no test covers a run that changes form.
6. **No solver test of the layer on a curved grid or across an $x_1$ split.**
   `heat_layer_deposits_flux_dt` is one Cartesian block.
7. **`body-heat` default band** `pmax` = 1 $\mathrm{Pa}$ (above).


[^env-heating]: Recorded run environment: Python 3.12.11, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0.

[^rg-74f4a55744e4]: thickness — the layer next to an x1 domain end that boundary heating or cooling is spread over, in x1 length units; given instead of depth

[^rg-6691bc383516]: $p$ — pressure [Pa]
